claim_map.scope: For every n≥1 and each prescribed real Jordan matrix J whose spectrum is entirely real, there exists a globally C∞ compactly supported real (1,1)-tensor L on ℝⁿ with Nijenhuis torsion zero. Its matrix is exactly J in a smooth commuting local frame on a nonempty open domain. Numerical eigenvalues, block sizes and grouping are prescribed, including repeated eigenvalues, nonsemisimple blocks and zero data.

For every globally smooth compactly supported real Nijenhuis operator on ℝⁿ, every eigenvalue at every point is real. The proof extends by zero to the one-point compactification Sⁿ and invokes the paper’s zero-point lemma grounded in prior local splitting/holomorphic theory.

For L=[[A(t),b(t)],[0,λ(t)]] in the global commuting angular/transverse frame of T^(n−1)×(−1,1), every angular torsion component vanishes and mixed torsion equals(A−λI)A′. Product order is essential; no separate condition on b′ or λ′ is imposed.

For any real-spectrum Jordan matrix in n≥2, designate one terminal vector transverse, retain its arrow in b, clear b, and process angular Jordan blocks. Move λ while A is fixed; then remove superdiagonal arrows in predecessor-first order, then move the scalar block with λ matched. Repeated/zero eigenvalues and singleton blocks are allowed; no division by spectral gaps. Smooth plateau reparameterizations permit gluing.

T^d embeds two-sidedly in ℝ^(d+1) by tubular induction with explicit trivial rank-two normal frame. The dimension-n collar around T^(n−1) carries the construction. q(t)=S(2(t²−1/16)) gives J on |t|≤1/4 and exactly zero on |t|≥3/4. The support is compactly contained in the open collar, so zero extension is smooth and torsion-free. n=1 is handled separately by scalar bump; J=0 is allowed.

On a closed connected smooth manifold, a real Nijenhuis operator vanishing at one point has entirely real spectrum. Proof takes a maximal positive imaginary part and maximal multiplicity, uses local splitting into a conjugate-pair block, holomorphic coefficients/maximum principle, then open-and-closed propagation. No gl-regularity, semisimplicity or real analyticity of the original tensor is assumed.

Credits nonreal obstruction, prior semisimple/two-dimensional examples, arbitrary-type point realizations and local splitting/holomorphic mechanisms. GeometryIII regular-layer and GeometryIV symmetry results are compared at their actual hypotheses. Finite controls corroborate indexing, not the universal geometric/analytic proof; no historical omitted-program replay or priority claim.

limitations: Classification of which Jordan types can be realized on some open domain, not a classification of all global Nijenhuis tensor fields up to equivalence.
The matrix is prescribed in a smooth commuting local frame, not in the fixed ambient Cartesian frame. The domain is chosen by the construction, not an arbitrary preassigned domain.
Type, rank and eigenvalues may change outside the realization region, and the operator becomes exactly zero. No everywhere-gl-regular or constant-global-type conclusion.
C∞ smooth construction only; no nonzero real-analytic compact-support result. The comparison GeometryIII theorem has additional analytic/gl-regular restrictions.
Necessity uses a closed connected manifold after compactification. The statement does not forbid local nonreal Nijenhuis models or nonreal spectrum on noncompact fields without compact support.
Finite mathematical controls do not prove the all-dimensional schedule, tubular embedding, gluing or maximum-principle argument. Scope executes no checker and issues no mathematical approval.
